_doc: THE HONESTY DEBT LEDGER. Every published falsehood, lapsed promise, and unverifiable claim the company currently carries, with a MACHINE-CHECKABLE done-condition for each. This is not a report — scripts/check-honesty-debt.mjs executes every `check` in this file and prints PAID or OWED. A `paid` entry that fails its own check is a REGRESSION and reds CI. `node scripts/check-honesty-debt.mjs --amplification-gate` exits 1 while any entry is owed, which is the doctrine 'credibility is a CLOSING asset — pay the honesty debt IN FULL before amplifying a single page of reach' expressed as an exit code instead of a paragraph.
_doctrine: docs/handoff/bones/phase-d-verdict.json; docs/handoff/bones/greats-free-authority.md line 36 (Michelin publishes demotions on schedule and does not apologize) and line 40 (a correction that names the gate now preventing recurrence is stronger evidence of integrity than never having erred).

_ownerLegend.agent: an agent session can complete this alone and verify it with the stated check
_ownerLegend.founder: requires a signature, a relationship, a market judgment, or an editorial decision no session can make
_ownerLegend.both: an agent prepares it; the founder decides or signs

_checkContract: `check` is a shell command run from the repo root named in `repo`. Exit 0 = PAID. Exit non-zero = OWED. A check that cannot be expressed as a command carries `check: null` and MUST carry `verifyBy` naming the human artifact that closes it.

items.title: The basis leak — a BLS index value published as $393.06/lb
items.what: feed.json published ground-beef at reference.priceUsd 393.06 with source 'bls' under basis 'wholesale', while cost-index/index.json published $5.51/lb for the same slug — 71x apart. The $393.06 is the BLS ground-beef index. data/cost-index.json labels every one of those observations basis:'index' at ingredients['ground-beef'].points[1].history[]; the basis was discarded at render by seriesJson() in scripts/build-cost-index-pages.mjs, which stamps the file with points[0].level.basis.
items.whyTheGateMissedIt: scripts/check-cost-index-basis-leak.mjs cross-referenced at the INGREDIENT level — 'does this slug have a dollar-basis newest level in the source?' Ground-beef does (usda-lmr, $5.51, wholesale, points[0]). One true statement about the ingredient waved through five false statements about observations.
items.fix: scripts/lib/basis.mjs now holds the render predicate (mayRenderAsDollars) imported by BOTH the renderer and the gate so they cannot drift; build-cost-index-pages.mjs mergedSeries() refuses any observation whose own basis or source cannot back a dollar, and PRINTS every suppression; the gate resolves every rendered $ back to its own observation via buildObservationModel().
items.gateAdded: scripts/check-cost-index-basis-leak.mjs (observation model + source registry + regime-break rail) and its --mutation-proof mode

items.title: The gate that could not be shown to fail
items.what: The basis-leak gate carried 22 green self-test assertions and ran green in CI throughout the period feed.json was publishing a 71x-wrong price. Every assertion was true. None was about the thing that was wrong. A gate that has never been shown to fail on the defect class it names is not evidence.
items.fix: --mutation-proof reintroduces each historical leak class into the LIVE on-disk data and asserts the gate goes RED, plus asserts the gate is GREEN on the unmutated baseline (or 'it went red' means nothing). Verified falsifiable on 2026-08-07 by flipping SOURCE_CAN_BACK_DOLLARS.bls to true: the proof dropped to 5/7 and named both toothless rails.

items.title: 165 `<!-- src: -->` citations with no gate behind them
items.what: 165 citation annotations, of which 138 name no file at all (they point at scripts/build-cost-index-dispatch.mjs's in-memory `dispatch` object, which exists only during a build) and 21 point at live rolling files the editions spine never froze. The founder named this gate 'rung 0' ten days ago; it was lost in a resume handoff and never written.
items.fix: scripts/check-src-sentinel.mjs parses every annotation, resolves it against the file it names, and hard-fails on a false claim. It defines the ANCHORED grammar `<!-- src: edition:<asOf> <path> = <value> -->` resolving against the append-only data/cost-index-editions.json, which is the structural fix: a dated post cites a frozen snapshot, not a moving file.
items.note: The GATE is paid. The 161 annotations it enumerates are HD-04 and are separately owed; the budget freezes them so no 166th can be added.

items.title: Repoint the July dispatch's 159 unverifiable citations at the frozen edition
items.what: 138 UNANCHORED + 21 DRIFT annotations. Each must become `edition:2026-07-06 <path> = <value>` resolving against data/cost-index-editions.json. Several paths the prose cites (risers[], fallers[], contributors[], pressure[]) are DERIVED at build time and are not in the spine — those fields must be frozen into the 2026-07-06 edition first.
items.fix: Work the queue in data/src-sentinel-worklist.json (regenerate with `node scripts/check-src-sentinel.mjs --worklist`). Lower data/src-sentinel-budget.json after each batch; the gate names the exact number to write.
items.doneWhen: data/src-sentinel-budget.json budgets.UNANCHORED === 0 and budgets.DRIFT === 0, with check-src-sentinel still exiting 0
items.effort: 2-3 agent sessions; the spine-freezing pass is the long pole

items.title: The line-852 cite drawer claims a CI check that did not exist
items.what: A reader-visible <details class="cite"> drawer states the cited files are 'both rebuilt from committed data on every refresh and re-checked in CI. Every number in this section traces to one of them.' No such gate existed, and the numbers in that very section are now false: pooledCoverage 0.772 vs a live 0.767, 32 items vs 75, 4,588 scored steps vs 79,086, overallHitRate 0.536 vs 0.506, 1,859 scored calls vs 34,029, a 2,080-entry revision ledger vs 10,294. This is a FALSE CLAIM ABOUT A GATE, in a PUBLIC repo, inside a drawer that invites verification — categorically worse for this brand than a stale number, because the page ships its own refutation recipe.
items.fix: The claim is now TRUE for the classes check-src-sentinel covers, but the numbers in that section are still wrong. Correct the section against the frozen 2026-07-06 edition, keep the drawer, and add the correction to the public ledger with the gate named.
items.verifyBy: The prose numbers in the #the-record section match data/cost-index-editions.json asOf 2026-07-06, the annotations are anchored (HD-04), and an entry exists in data/cost-index-corrections.json naming check-src-sentinel.mjs as the gate added.
items.founderReason: Correcting a published market read is an editorial judgment. The choice between correct-in-place and retract is the founder's; the recommendation of record is correct-in-place with a dated notice, because a retraction removes the evidence of the fix.
items.effort: 60-90 founder minutes once HD-04 has frozen the edition fields

items.title: ground-beef's series now reads current and is not
items.what: FOUND BY the HD-01 repair. Suppressing the five BLS index observations left a file stamped asOf 2026-06-10 whose newest observation is 2024-01-05 — 887 days older. Ground-beef's ENTIRE live history is index-basis; its only dollar level ($5.51 usda-lmr, 2026-06-10) sits in points[].level and never reaches entry.history, which is what mergedSeries() reads. One lie was replaced with a different one.
items.fix: Either (a) plumb the LMR level into entry.history so the series carries its real dollar point, or (b) mark ground-beef as coverage-limited and null its asOf the way a retired series does. This is a data-plumbing decision, not something a gate should invent.
items.gateAdded: check-cost-index-basis-leak.mjs staleSeries channel — reports any series whose asOf outruns its newest observation by >60 days
items.doneWhen: the gate's staleSeries channel reports 0 series
items.effort: 1 agent session to plumb; a founder call on which option

items.title: The warrant canary is 89 days lapsed and was never published anywhere
items.what: 'Last updated and signed: 2026-05-10' against 2026-08-07 = 89 days. Its own cadence section says the statement is updated on the first of each month; 06-01, 07-01 and 08-01 are all missed. Its own text says 'if the warrant canary disappears or stops being updated on schedule, draw your own conclusions.' The signature block still contains the literal placeholder. The live privacy policy links to a URL that does not exist. A warrant canary is the one artifact whose failure mode is inverted: read literally by exactly the privacy-attentive buyer this product targets, it currently signals the event it exists to disclose.
items.fix: Pick ONE, today. (a) RETIRE: delete the file and record an ADR saying a one-person pre-revenue company will not commit to a monthly signing cadence it cannot keep — honest and defensible. (b) SHIP: re-sign with the real key, publish at a real URL, and gate the date.
items.verifyBy: Either docs/warrant-canary.md is deleted with an ADR recording the retirement, or its 'Last updated and signed' date is within 35 days AND a check-warrant-canary-fresh.mjs gate is wired.
items.founderReason: A signature cannot be delegated. This is the single item on this ledger that is definitionally founder-only.
items.effort: either 10 minutes (retire) or 30 minutes (sign + publish) + 1 agent session for the gate

items.title: There is no public ledger of Muntin's own published errors
items.what: data/cost-revisions.json holds 10,294 entries — but those are SOURCE revisions, someone else's number changing. Nothing logs a number MUNTIN published and got wrong. For a company selling 'it holds a number back rather than print a guess', that is the one ledger that buys trust, and it is the only one missing.

items.title: The storefront deploy exits 1 — five (idem) builders verified but never run
items.what: check-all runs inside the Cloudflare deploy command and reaches 312 of 320 before failing on builders that check-idem-coverage verifies but that nothing in build.command re-runs — so ordinary data drift turns into a red deploy no automation can clear. Recorded here because a company that cannot deploy cannot ship a correction, which makes this a prerequisite for every other item on this ledger.
items.fix: For each failing builder: add it to build.command, or move it to check-idem-coverage's MANUAL registry with who runs it and when it drifts. The gate already demands one or the other.
items.check: node scripts/check-idem-coverage.mjs && node scripts/check-gate-coverage.mjs && test -f data/deploy-green-receipt.json && node -e "const r=require('./data/deploy-green-receipt.json'); process.exit((Date.now()-Date.parse(r.verifiedOn))/86400000<14 && r.exitCode===0?0:1)"
items.doneWhen: A dated receipt at data/deploy-green-receipt.json records `node scripts/check-all.mjs` exiting 0, verified within the last 14 days. Write it with: node scripts/check-all.mjs; echo '{"verifiedOn":"YYYY-MM-DD","exitCode":0,"passed":"N of N"}' > data/deploy-green-receipt.json
items.checkNote: Twice-corrected, both times by running the ledger rather than reading it. (1) First written as check-idem-coverage.mjs, which PASSES — flagged SURPRISE on the first run; idem-coverage verifies every (idem) builder is run by SOMETHING, not that check-all is green. (2) Then written as check-all.mjs itself — which is RECURSION, because check-honesty-debt.mjs is wired INTO check-all. It hung the gate. A ledger that executes its own items must never invoke the orchestrator that executes it. The check is now a dated RECEIPT of a green check-all run, which is bounded, honest, and cannot recurse.

items.title: 24 gates stay green when their own declared inputs are corrupted
items.what: MEASURED, not inferred. scripts/audit-gate-teeth.mjs corrupts each gate's declared data/*.json input (every number x3+7, every boolean inverted, every date blanked) and runs the gate. 24 of 128 stay GREEN. The prior audit's claim of ~56 tautologies in check-all was reached by reading script headers — which is exactly how check-cost-index-basis-leak.mjs got its reputation while publishing a 71x-wrong price. This list was produced by breaking things and watching.
items.fix: Per gate, one of three: (a) it guards HTML or a structural property the mutation preserves — record that in its header and it is fine; (b) it is a genuine tautology — DELETE it and remove its check-all entry, which is how the net gate count goes down; (c) it should have teeth and does not — fix the assertion. Work highest-traffic first. The 2 ALREADY-RED gates (check-cost-index-orphans, check-removed-slugs) are unmeasurable until they are green and are part of HD-13.
items.gateAdded: scripts/audit-gate-teeth.mjs — deliberately NOT wired into check-all, because it mutates working-tree files and a gate that edits the repo has no business inside a deploy. Run by hand, quarterly.
items.doneWhen: every NO-TEETH gate in data/gate-teeth-audit.json is deleted, fixed, or has a header stating why the mutation cannot reach what it guards — then re-run `node scripts/audit-gate-teeth.mjs --json`
items.effort: 3-4 agent sessions, one batch of 6-8 gates each
